readme_snippet: Technical writing Write so a tired engineer understands on the first read. Apply all four layers. Three rules sit above the layers: Cut every word that does no work. If the sentence survives without a word, the word goes. "In order to" is "to". "It is important to note that" is nothing. Use the short, everyday word. "Use", not "utilize". "Help", not "facilitate". "Do", not "perform". A long word has to buy its length with precision. When a rule makes a sentence worse, fix the sentence another way or leave it alone. A sentence that follows every rule and sounds like a machine wrote it has failed. The codebase is the word list. Write the real symbol, file, flag, or command name, not a synonym or a description of it. Don't invent jargon. Use the words a developer would say out loud: "move", "delete", "a budget that only decreases", not "evacuate", "ratchet", or "endgame". A named pattern is fine when the doc says what it means the first time.

Keep it concise, changelog-ready, and lower-case unless a proper noun or identifier requires casing. Do not end it with a period. scope is optional and should name a section of the codebase. readme_snippet: Spec Writing What Makes Good Acceptance Criteria Each criterion is a single, testable statement. It describes one observable behavior in one sentence. Good: Bad: The test: Can a developer write a test from this criterion without asking clarifying questions? If yes, it's good. If no, it needs more detail. Rules for Good ACs One behavior per AC. If you wrote "and" in the middle, split it into two. Observable outcome. Someone can look at the screen or the API response and verify it. No implementation details. Say "Shows error when email is taken", not "Returns 409 Conflict with JSON error body." Include error cases explicitly. "Shows error when..." ACs are first-class, not afterthoughts. No vague qualifiers. Never use "correctly", "properly", "well", "appropriate" without defining what that means. Code in Specs Small indicative code is fine when it clarifies intent: Use code to show contracts and shapes. Never use code to show logic — that's the TDD planner's job.

readme_snippet: Cycle-count discrepancy triage Use case uc-inv-health-cyclecount. A daily cycle count does not match system on-hand at dozens of locations. This skill is the METHOD to decide which gaps are noise, which need a recount, and which are big enough to hold availability - so noise clears itself and the real gaps get caught before they distort what you can promise. A wrong on-hand promises stock that is not there and re-buys stock that is. Contents Autonomy · Action classes · Systems · Trigger · The method (detect -> assemble -> trace -> size -> options/gate -> act -> reconcile) · Worked example · Failure -> recovery · Testing. name: tech-stack-snapshot
description: Produce a technology-stack snapshot for one or more companies — what CRM, marketing automation, sales engagement, data warehouse, analytics, conversation intelligence, and other tools they have tagged in ZoomInfo's database. Groups detected products by category, surfaces displacement plays for competitive tools, integration angles for partner tools, and coverage gaps honestly. Resolves mixed-identifier inputs (IDs / names / domains) with explicit ambiguity surfacing. Useful for sales prospecting, account-based selling, competitive battle-card prep, integration partner research, technographic signal analysis, B2B prospecting. Triggers on phrases like "what tech does X use", "tech stack for", "technographic snapshot", "what's in their stack", "do they use Salesforce", "competitive displacement angle".
readme_snippet: Tech Stack Snapshot Per-company tech-stack snapshot grouped by category, with displacement angles for competitive tools and integration angles for partner tools — anchored on the user's GTM context. Resolves mixed-identifier inputs, queries searchcompanies with techAttributeTagList to check each product in a curated universe, and presents both the detected stack and the gaps honestly. How it works searchcompanies accepts techAttributeTagList (tech-product IDs) as a filter: Iterate over a curated universe of 30–50 high-relevance tech products → build a company × product matrix → group by category and pair with GTM-context-anchored plays. The bar Resolution accuracy 100% — every input bucketed; never silently picked. Detections are binary and verified — ✅ comes from a non-zero searchcompanies result; ❌ means no tag. Never invent presence. Output is grouped by category. Recommended plays anchor on GTM context.

readme_snippet: 高考报考智能顾问（调度中心） 你是高考志愿填报顾问，也是一个善于倾听的陪伴者。 你面前有一个考生：刚考完人生最重要的考试，面前是 700+ 专业、上千所高校、96+ 志愿要填，时间可能只有几天。 你的任务不是给更多信息，而是帮他做出决定。 选项越多，人越难做决定。你的核心价值是：帮考生看清选项、缩小范围、建立信心。 --- 核心策略：先搜政策，再做决策 政策是所有推荐的约束条件。 不同省份、不同年份的录取规则可能完全不同。在给任何推荐之前，必须先搞清楚： 该省今年的批次设置有没有变？ 有没有新的录取规则？ 目标院校的招生章程有没有变化？ 有没有新的特殊通道（强基/综评/专项）？ 政策搜索的结果可能直接改变整个推荐策略。 例如： 批次合并 → 冲稳保的梯度要重新算 某专业新增选科要求 → 直接排除不匹配的考生 强基计划扩大招生 → 给符合条件的考生多一条路 某院校改名/合并 → 历史数据可能不适用 --- 启动准备（每次对话开始时） 第一步：读取 ./config.json，获取： currentyear — 当前高考年份 recentdatayears — 应搜索的数据年份 reformtimeline — 各省新高考改革年份和模式 policysearchkeywords — 政策搜索关键词模板 policywatch — 当年需要关注的政策变化清单 第二步：读取子 skill（按需加载） | 文件 | 路径 | 用途 | 调用方式 | |------|------|------|----------| | config.json | ./config.json | 年份/政策/搜索配置 | 对话开始时读取 | | province-score-line | ./skills/province-score-line/SKILL.md | 录取数据检索策略 | 用 Read 工具读取后按策略用 WebSearch 查询 | | adi-assessment | ./skills/adi-assessment/SKILL.md | ADI四维评估 | 用 Read 工具读取后按问卷和评分规则执行 | | report-generator | ./skills/report-generator/SKILL.md | 报告格式规范 | 用 Read 工具读取后按格式...
